title: The spires thinned out — and the landscape, with no stitching in it
question: Are the spires occasional enough now, or still too many? And does this read as one landscape — I need to know whether the "hard boundary" complaint survives once the picture stops lying.
context_md:
**First: your #1 issue was my picture, not the world, and I am sorry for the round it cost.**

The card you judged was three viewport shots from *different parts of the world* butted together with no separator — tiles at world x 1109-1620, 3840-4351 and 6570-7081, with **2,219 unshown columns between each**. So the "repeating hard boundary at 1/3 and 2/3" was the seam between them. Measured: those two joins were the **largest and second-largest of all 1,535 adjacent column pairs** in that image, and the skyline stepped **61 rows in one column** across the first. For scale, I then measured the real thing — the largest step worldgen produces anywhere, in any preset, is **5 rows**. The seam was twelve times bigger than anything the generator can make.

Both panes here are one **contiguous** strip, world x 1109-2645 unbroken, same moment, no joins. `viewshot` grew a `strip=1` mode and a white gutter for the old kind, and the summary line now names the columns it is *not* showing.

**The gnome is in it, as you asked.** He is 7x14 and standing on the ground in each third — the counts below were taken with him out of frame, because he is 14 rows proud over 7 columns and my spire detector counts him as a spire.

**The spires.** `residual_density` 1.4 -> 0.45, chosen from a sweep rather than by arithmetic, measured as spires per 512-column screen over 48 screens and **paired against residuals-switched-off** — which mattered: at my first threshold half of canyon's standing features were still there with the pass disabled. They are boulders and brow lips. I would have been tuning the wrong pass.

On this exact span, one variable, gnome out of frame: **8 spires [6,1,1] per screen -> 4 [3,1,0]**, and the cluster of three tall monuments (50, 44 and 57 rows within 300 columns) is now a single 57.

**What I could not settle from the diff:** whether "occasional" means what I have, or fewer still. 0.3 measures identically to 0.45, so there is room to go further at no cost if these are still too many.

**Also changed in both panes** (so it is not the variable here): the sand lenses are no longer perfect ovals. There is a separate card for those at proper zoom.
